basis: Source-grounded review criteria frozen before responses; revisable expectations, not absolute gold annotations. Judge explicit meaning separately from evidence-only retention and graph validity.
names: definition
Material discrepancy excludes changes defined as immaterial in the cited remote section.
explain
Applicant must explain discrepancies across application and citizenship/nationality and identity evidence.
options
Documentation duty retains one-or-more grouping and all six leaf document alternatives.
remote_exception
Married-name exception remains qualified by unavailable cited text, not a blanket exemption.
counterfeiting
Evidence must be reviewed for counterfeiting or alteration.
previous_name
Previous-name prohibition retains after-material-change scope and documentary-permission exception with correct target.
identity
Name-as-identity fact and possible evidence requirement retain factual versus possible force.
suspension
Suspension duty retains more-than-one-year, DS-11 and unchanged-ID case.
emergency
Emergency permission retains the same three limits plus insufficient time before urgent/emergency travel.
explanation
Generally-needed documentation remains explanatory, not a prerequisite of notation.
notation
Fully notate before return, including seen and returned and IRL; deadline is not a prerequisite of notation itself.
recent_change
Within-one-year DS-11 exemption and unchanged-ID conditional documentation duty remain separately referenceable.
date_role
CT header date does not establish an effective date for every extracted rule.
photos: Closed eyes acceptable for infants, particularly newborns, without narrowing to newborns only.
Discreet head support and head tilt allowances remain separately referenceable; car seat is an example.
Parent face prohibited in infant photograph.
Photo noncompliance triggers requesting a new photograph without importing infant-only scope.
Color is mandatory; six-month recency and likeness retain should.
Hairstyle/facial-hair difference acceptable if still good likeness; does not waive recency.
May wish to reuse is descriptive possibility, not an unconditional permission.
Recently issued certificate does not ensure photo recency due to processing times; retain caution without false applicability link.
leave: eligibility
Covered-employer eligibility preserves all three cumulative conditions: at least 12 months, 1250 hours in immediately preceding 12 months, and 50 employees within 75 miles.
remote
Airline-flight-crew special-hours and outside-US references remain unresolved without invented content.
nonconsecutive
12 employment months need not be consecutive, subject to the stated counting rules.
seven_years
Periods before breaks of seven years or more need not count, subject to b2 exceptions; preserve source difference from more than seven years in b2.
prior_service
Prior periods before more-than-seven-year breaks must count under either USERRA-service or written-rehire-agreement alternative.
military_absence
USERRA-covered absence itself also counts toward 12 months; no greater entitlement than USERRA.
agreement
Written rehire agreement includes collective bargaining; education/childrearing are examples, not exhaustive conditions.
payroll_week
Any part of a week on payroll counts, including stated paid/unpaid leave cases with benefits or compensation.
52_weeks
52 weeks equals 12 months specifically for intermittent/occasional/casual employment assessment.
voluntary_credit
Employer may count earlier service after a continuous break over seven years; if choosing to, must act uniformly for all employees with similar breaks.
baggage: Accessible-person/property prohibition retains all three alternative screening/sterile-area/boarding settings and paragraph-b qualification.
All three paragraph-b categories exempt firearms/other weapons from paragraph a only, not explosives/incendiaries or checked-baggage restrictions.
Checked-baggage prohibitions also cover baggage in inaccessible cargo hold under cited section.
Loaded firearms remain prohibited; unloaded-firearm exceptions do not waive this rule.

Unloaded-firearm rule preserves all four cumulative conditions, including declaration before checking, oral-or-written alternative, hard-sided container, locked container, and only-passenger key/combination.
Unauthorized explosive/incendiary prohibition retains unauthorized qualifier and checked/inaccessible-hold scope.
This section does not prohibit ammunition in checked baggage or same firearm container; additional part-175 requirements remain a reference, not invented permission free of other rules.
